theme: permutation and achievable-fit calibration of Sanskrit lexical windows
question: Do the October 9 Bonta-extension lexical statistics depend on which Wells codes carry which Sanskrit seed values, and do the new anchor codes open more windows than frequency-matched codes?
outcome: The 362 searched and 274 multi-context codes are identical in every rearrangement. Nonempty full intersections are 164 against 158.0 +/- 10.5 (p = 0.28; annealed 255); repeated exact residuals 201 against 208.0 +/- 13.0 (p = 0.74; annealed 264). Moving the 17 new anchors to frequency-matched codes gives 395 +/- 175 windows against 256. Each code's best residual keeps its published support under rearrangement; the post-outcome residuals sam, sa and ati lose support when the anchor values move.
challenge: A cached reimplementation first disagreed with the frozen search because its normalization is not idempotent, and the first annealer was too slow on a shared machine.
remedy: Exact agreement with the frozen lexical_search on four assignments, per-window caches and incremental counters checked against fresh searches, and separate null, anneal and summary stages.
retry_when: A lexical criterion with measured redundancy, such as held-out likelihood under the claimed language, replaces dictionary completion, or seed values come from evidence independent of the corpus windows.
